prompt:
Draft a procedure for control of nonconforming outputs at a CNC machining facility. Cover detection methods (in-process inspection, final inspection, customer returns), segregation requirements, disposition authority, rework/re-inspection, and concession process. Align with ISO 9001 clause 8.7.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "1. PURPOSE
This procedure establishes the requirements for the identification, segregation, evaluation, and disposition of nonconforming outputs at the CNC machining facility to ensure nonconforming products are controlled and do not reach the customer unless authorized. This procedure aligns with ISO 9001:2015 Clause 8.7.

2. SCOPE
Applies to all in-process, final inspection, and customer return outputs from CNC machining operations, including raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished parts.

3. DEFINITIONS
- Nonconforming Output: A product or service that does not meet specified requirements.
- Segregation: Physical isolation of nonconforming outputs to prevent unintended use or delivery.
- Rework: Action taken to make a nonconforming output conform to requirements.
- Concession: Formal approval for use or release of a nonconforming output under specified conditions.
- Disposition Authority: Designated personnel authorized to decide on the disposition of nonconforming outputs.

4. RESPONSIBILITIES
- Operators: Detect and report nonconformities during operation.
- Quality Inspectors: Perform in-process and final inspections; document nonconformities.
- Production Supervisors: Initiate segregation and notify Quality Department.
- Quality Manager: Authorize disposition decisions and concession requests.
- Customer Service: Manage customer returns and communicate feedback to Quality.

5. DETECTION METHODS
5.1 In-Process Inspection: Operators and quality inspectors use calibrated gauges, CMMs, and visual checks at critical process steps. Nonconformities are recorded on In-Process Inspection Reports (Form Q-IP-001).
5.2 Final Inspection: Finished parts are inspected per approved work instructions and drawing specifications. Nonconforming outputs are flagged on Final Inspection Report (Form Q-FI-002).
5.3 Customer Returns: Customer complaints or returned parts are logged in the Customer Return Log (Form Q-CR-003) and investigated by Quality for root cause.

6. SEGREGATION REQUIREMENTS
All nonconforming outputs must be immediately segregated from conforming product using:
- Red tags with unique nonconformance ID
- Designated quarantine area with locked access
- Clear labeling: "NONCONFORMING - DO NOT USE"
Segregation must occur within 1 hour of detection. No nonconforming output may be moved or processed without authorization.

7. DISPOSITION AUTHORITY
Disposition decisions are authorized by the Quality Manager or designated delegate. Only personnel with documented training in ISO 9001 Clause 8.7 may approve disposition. All decisions must be documented on the Nonconforming Output Disposition Form (Form Q-NCD-004).

8. REWORK AND RE-INSPECTION
8.1 Rework: Nonconforming outputs may be reworked if feasible and approved. Rework must follow approved procedures and be documented.
8.2 Re-inspection: After rework, the output must be fully re-inspected by Quality using the same criteria as initial inspection. Re-inspection results must be recorded and linked to the original nonconformance ID.
8.3 If rework fails, the output must be re-evaluated for alternative disposition.

9. CONCESSION PROCESS
9.1 A concession request may be initiated for nonconforming outputs that cannot be reworked but are deemed acceptable for use under controlled conditions.
9.2 The request must include:
- Description of nonconformity
- Risk assessment
- Customer notification (if applicable)
- Justification for release
9.3 Concessions require written approval from the Quality Manager and, if applicable, the customer. Approved concessions are documented on Form Q-NCD-004 and tracked for audit purposes.
9.4 Concessions are not permitted for safety-critical features without explicit customer and regulatory approval.

10. RECORD KEEPING
All nonconformance reports, disposition forms, rework records, and concession approvals must be retained for a minimum of 5 years.

11. REVIEW AND IMPROVEMENT
The Quality Manager shall review nonconforming output trends quarterly. Corrective actions shall be initiated via the CAPA procedure (QMS-008) for recurring issues.

12. REFERENCES
- ISO 9001:2015 Clause 8.7
- QMS-008: Corrective Action Procedure
- Q-IP-001: In-Process Inspection Report
- Q-FI-002: Final Inspection Report
- Q-CR-003: Customer Return Log
- Q-NCD-004: Nonconforming Output Disposition Form",
